items.title: Surjectivity of the restriction map in Galois cohomology from an imaginary quadratic extension to the real place for a connected semisimple algebraic group over the rationals
items.author: Dave Witte Morris
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the lemma at source lines 245-249, label KneserHasse: for a connected semisimple algebraic group G over the rationals and any imaginary quadratic extension L, the natural restriction map from H^1(L/Q; G(L)) to H^1(R; G) is surjective. The proof retained at source lines 251-282 is the author's own argument rather than a citation: it represents an arbitrary real cohomology class by an element t of a maximal torus with t t^sigma = 1 and uses weak approximation for the variety of maximal tori to make that torus rational, then passes to the restriction of scalars R = Res_{L/Q} T, exhibits the L-isomorphism R = T x T that turns the norm-one condition r r^tau = 1 into an explicitly described subtorus, proves that this subtorus is defined over Q, and finishes by moving the class along a rational point produced by weak approximation at the infinite place. The non-routine content is exactly this combination: the cohomological representative has to be replaced by a rational point lying in the same connected component of a norm-one torus, which needs both the explicit model of the restriction of scalars and the archimedean density statement. Neither surjectivity nor the existence of such a representative follows from the definitions of Galois cohomology or from formal Hasse-principle arguments alone.
